‘We cannot ignore the elephant in the room’: Ken Paxton’s estranged wife speaks to GOP women | CNN Politics

Angela Paxton, who is divorcing Texas Republican Senate nominee Ken Paxton, posted a video Monday of recent remarks urging Republican women to support GOP candidates in Texas this fall even if they have reservations about them.

Actual Article Body:
Angela Paxton, who is divorcing Texas Republican Senate nominee Ken Paxton, posted a video Monday of recent remarks urging Republican women to support GOP candidates in Texas this fall even if they have reservations about them.

In the speech, titled “The Elephant in the Room,” Angela Paxton, a Texas state senator, did not mention her husband or his hotly contested race against Democrat James Talarico. But she made multiple references to Texas Republicans feeling conflicted about how to vote in the November election, particularly amid Ken Paxton’s long history of legal and ethical controversies.

Angela Paxton filed for divorce last year from the state’s attorney general and cited “biblical grounds,” accusing him of adultery.

Woman finds recovery at home for women battling addiction

An Indiana woman shares how she broke away from addiction after years of drug use.

Actual Article Body:
NEW ALBANY, Ind. (Aging Untold) — A recovery home in New Albany, Indiana, called The Breakaway, is helping women break away from addiction, and one woman who says it helped her find her way back is sharing her story.

Erin Wyatt said life felt like a roller coaster and she lost all sight of reality.

She started using drugs while she was in high school and said she was doing cocaine in the bathroom stalls at school.

The drug abuse continued for years and got worse. Wyatt said she started using ecstasy, acid and ketamine, known as designer drugs, along with nitrous, an inhalant.

When she started using methamphetamine intravenously, psychosis set in, along with homelessness, she said.

In all, Wyatt said she’s probably been to jail 10 times.

She stopped thinking about her children and let other people care for them, which was for the best, she said.

Her oldest daughter stayed with Wyatt’s grandparents while she gave her youngest daughter up for adoption.
